findings.title: Compute the bound once, not for every declaration
findings.summary: Repeated whole-book work explained a large part of checking time.
findings.mechanism: Chronological law fills repeatedly scanned all preceding definitions to compute a fresh binder bound. Computing that bound once removed repeated scans while preserving declaration visibility as a separate semantic responsibility.
limits: Timing measures the combined P9 release, including smaller checking/equality repairs; it is not isolated attribution to one helper.
The source differs between phase benchmark windows.

visual.before: Every fill → scan the book again

findings.title: Keep literals compact until structure is needed
findings.summary: A smaller representation prevents copying, freshening and serialization work from being created.
findings.mechanism: Expanded numeric and string literals created constructor trees that downstream passes repeatedly traversed. Compact literal nodes retain the value and provide an on-demand constructor view, with quantity presence, literal/constructor identity and specialization keys preserved.

impact.scope: structural census, separate from final release timing

limits: The structural census and final timing use separately identified source snapshots; they are not the same run.
The P16 release also integrates frontend changes; source grows by 1,057 physical lines from P15.

visual.before: Literal → large constructor tree → repeated copies
visual.after: Compact literal → constructor view only on demand

findings.title: Write the loop the existing emitter can see
findings.summary: Equivalent source shapes can have very different allocation costs.
findings.mechanism: Passing a Boolean to a small lookup worker lets recursive membership and lookup lower into a mutual tail loop. This avoids per-miss branch closures and trampoline messages. Reusing already checked constructor structure removes further work.
limits: Combined release effects do not isolate one helper.
This is a reproducible source-shape finding, not proof of an upstream emitter bug.
The larger P13 selector prototype was deferred despite its 10.6% screen gain.

findings.title: Give each semantic result one owner
findings.summary: Sharing existing mechanisms reduced maintenance burden without inventing a new abstraction layer.
findings.mechanism: The cleanup removed obsolete algorithms, reused the real loader trace for provenance, and returned one structured checker result instead of replaying a failure. P19 then routed ordinary code and live instances through one checker and one source-event order.

impact.scope: P19 vs immediately preceding prefix repair

limits: Line count is a size proxy, not a score for conceptual complexity.
S4 removed 830 physical lines of duplicate law/fill declarations; 405 were blank separators.
P19 removes 475 lines vs its immediate installed predecessor, or 473 vs the selected P17/18 checkpoint.
Later correctness and performance work added source; latest P36 has 18,174 lines.

findings.title: Parse with the context the language actually needs
findings.summary: One contextual frontend closed the remaining measured gaps and retired duplicate scope reconstruction.
findings.mechanism: The reference parser needs lexical information at specific points. A mostly context-free parse followed by scope and alias replay could change which error appears first. Actual lexical state and one materializer align semantic checkpoints and preserve error order.
limits: The first candidate was 32.8% slower; profiling, guarded lookups and a constructor index recovered that regression.
977 gross retired block lines are not the net saving: the whole compiler shrank by 300 lines, while bytes increased 0.57%.
Exact finite frontend comparison does not prove universal language equivalence.

findings.title: Use the index to prove work is unnecessary
findings.summary: An index can skip absent-name scans while preserving chronological lookup semantics.
findings.mechanism: A scope-index miss proves a local name absent, so the original scan can be skipped. An index hit retains the original first-event lookup because indexes can pick different duplicate-name winners. A direct Boolean membership worker removes additional per-miss overhead.
limits: The release adds 28 lines and three helpers; it introduces no new representation, cache or module.
Three observations per image on one machine are not general speed guarantees.

visual.after: index miss → skip; index hit → preserve original scan

findings.title: Keep the investigation loop short
findings.summary: A checked bootstrap and focused differential controls made small hypotheses practical to test.
findings.mechanism: Full self-reproduction remained an integration exercise. Routine edits instead built a checked bootstrap compiler and ran focused comparison cases, keeping feedback in tens of seconds while broad suites and self-reproduction supplied separate evidence.

impact.scope: P1; different task from focused loop

limits: 39.45 minutes for self-reproduction versus tens of seconds for a focused loop changes the validation task; it is not a same-task 90× speedup.
These development observations are not an exclusive controlled timing series.
